hints: Look at the percentage data first and turn it into a simple atomic ratio to get the empirical formula.
Notice the broad, strong dip around 3200 to 3400 cm-1 in the IR, and check what is missing around 1700 cm-1 where C=O would appear.
Combine the empirical formula C3H6O with the IR evidence for an alcohol and no carbonyl to pick the structure that fits both.
walkthrough:
**Find the empirical formula from percentages**

Assume 100 g of T, then convert each % to moles. This gives the simplest whole number ratio.

$$\frac{62.07}{12.0} = 5.17 \text{ mol C}, \quad \frac{10.34}{1.0} = 10.34 \text{ mol H}, \quad \frac{27.59}{16.0} = 1.72 \text{ mol O}$$

$$\text{C} : \text{H} : \text{O} = \frac{5.17}{1.72} : \frac{10.34}{1.72} : \frac{1.72}{1.72} = 3 : 6 : 1$$ So empirical formula is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$.

**Read the IR spectrum for functional groups**

There is a broad, strong absorption centred near 3300 cm-1. That is classic for hydrogen bonded O-H in an alcohol.

There is no strong absorption near 1700 cm-1. That means there is no $\text{C=O}$ group, so no carboxylic acid and no ketone or aldehyde.

**Match composition and IR to the structures**

Option A, cyclohexane-1,4-diol, is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$, which simplifies to $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$. It has two alcohol OH groups and no C=O, fitting both tests perfectly.

Strong absorptions near 1000 to 1100 cm-1 also support C-O of an alcohol. So T must be the diol ring structure.

options.A: Cyclohexane-1,4-diol is C6H12O2, empirical C3H6O, matching 62.07% C, 10.34% H, 27.59% O. It contains alcohol OH groups giving the broad O-H stretch near 3300 cm-1 and C-O near 1050 cm-1, with no C=O near 1700 cm-1, exactly as the spectrum shows.
options.B: 3-methylpentanoic acid is also C6H12O2 so it matches the percentages, but it is a carboxylic acid. It would show a very broad O-H from 2500 to 3000 cm-1 and a strong sharp C=O near 1710 cm-1, which is absent in the spectrum.
options.C: Propanone is C3H6O so it matches the empirical formula, but it is a ketone with no O-H. It would show a strong C=O near 1715 cm-1 and no broad alcohol O-H near 3300 cm-1, the opposite of the observed spectrum.
options.D: Hexane-1,6-diol is C6H14O2, empirical C3H7O, not C3H6O. Its calculated %H is about 11.9%, too high for the given 10.34%. Although its IR would show alcohol O-H, it fails the elemental analysis test.
